transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-25
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam Patel (Redwood SE), Janelle Ortiz (Redwood CSM); Sofia Martinez (Aperture Labs), Ethan Cole (Aperture Labs), Priya Nair (Aperture Labs)
Shared: QBR deck (link), latest infra diagram (link), billing export CSV (link)

Summary: quick QBR focused on usage trends, cost drivers, reliability incidents last quarter, and roadmap alignment. Agreed to test a dedicated pool for peak inference and to run a KV cache benchmark to validate token cost reductions.

00:00 Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining; can you hear me ok?
00:08 Sofia Martinez: yep all good, thanks Maya.
00:12 Maya Chen: cool, quick agenda — usage and cost trends, reliability incidents, roadmap and recommendations, and then next steps. We'll go 45 minutes.
01:02 Liam Patel: just to flag from the SE side I'll talk through some performance numbers and the KV cache suggestions we ran last week, there's a couple of things that might change your unit cost materially.
01:26 Priya Nair: great, that's what we're most interested in — costs. Our CFO is asking about cost per embedding and tail latency impacts.
02:10 Ethan Cole: and from infra we care about autoscaling, burst capacity, and the VPC peering we set up — any changes there could affect throughput.

03:00 Maya Chen: thanks, Sofia — quick question: what's your top success metric for this quarter? Is it cost reduction, latency SLOs, or feature rollout?
03:12 Sofia Martinez: top is reliability right now; we had two outages in February that impacted our chat and summarization flows. Secondarily, cost, yes.
03:29 Janelle Ortiz: we logged both incidents, we have notes in the ticketing system; I'll share those after the call.

05:00 Usage & Cost review
05:05 Maya Chen: looking at your usage, embeddings are up 42% month-over-month; generation calls are flat. Most of the rise is nightly batch jobs for semantic search index updates. That's driving tokens and embedding units.
05:29 Sofia Martinez: right, the nightly reindex grew because product launched two new pipelines. We expected it but not the cost delta.
06:00 Liam Patel: a quick thing — your batch job is calling the full context model with longer sequences. If you switch to the optimized embedding model and shard batches, we saw up to 3x throughput improvement in similar workloads.
06:18 Priya Nair: when you say optimized embedding model, is that a different model family? What's the quality delta?
06:28 Liam Patel: it's a smaller distilled embedder Redwood verifies; quality delta is negligible for your search precision based on the eval set you shared, but cost per embedding is about 60% lower.
06:45 Sofia Martinez: that's promising. Can you share the eval results?
06:50 Liam Patel: yes, we'll attach the eval spreadsheet.

08:10 Reliability incidents
08:15 Maya Chen: do you have the incident timeline, Sofia?
08:20 Sofia Martinez: yes — Feb 11 around 03:40 UTC chat latency spiked, error rates 502s for ~18 minutes; Feb 24 the nightly index job failed due to timeouts for 45 minutes. Both aligned with peak repro loads.
08:40 Janelle Ortiz: from Redwood logs, there was a simultaneous autoscaler cooldown that limited burst capacity; we recommended a temporary bump during your index window.
08:52 Ethan Cole: we were on the shared pool at the time; would Dedicated have avoided that?
09:05 Maya Chen: likely yes, Dedicated gives reserved throughput and isolates from noisy neighbors. It also supports configurable burst policies.
09:12 Priya Nair: what's the SLA on Dedicated?
09:18 Maya Chen: our Dedicated offering has 99.95% uptime SLA and a latency target for per-token generation; we'll include specifics in the proposal.

11:00 Performance deep-dive (SE-led)
11:05 Liam Patel: ok pulling up the numbers — your  p50 is ~120ms for short chat messages, p95 sits at 480ms, and p99 spikes to 1.2s during peak. For embeddings the p95 is fine but batch job timeouts come from single-threaded reindexers not auto-sharded.
11:35 Ethan Cole: 1.2s p99 is rough. Can we get that under 700ms without big cost increases?
11:45 Liam Patel: yes — options: enable prefix KV cache for common conversation prompts, reduce context window for small assistant prompts, or move heavy nightly reindex to a Dedicated pool with larger instance sizing. Each has tradeoffs.
12:10 Priya Nair: what about quantization? We heard Redwood supports int8/4 quantized variants. Any impact on quality for our models?
12:24 Liam Patel: we have quantization profiles; for embedding models int8 gives negligible quality loss, for some generation models int4 can be OK but needs eval. We can recommend a quantized variant for test on your workload.

15:00 Billing anomalies and cost drivers
15:05 Maya Chen: we noticed a spike on Mar 3 for a client-facing demo — long generation runs with verbose prompts. That accounted for ~7% of the last month's overage.
15:20 Sofia Martinez: ah yes that was the demo to investors; we didn't think it would run so many requests. Any guardrails?
15:28 Janelle Ortiz: we can enable per-route quotas and token caps; also set alerting on unusual spend per API key.
15:40 Ethan Cole: can we do predictive estimates for commits? Like if we move to Dedicated, how do we size?
15:50 Maya Chen: we have a sizing worksheet — we'll run a model based on your traffic profiles. For commit sizing we recommend a 3-month runway and then the ability to scale.

18:10 Roadmap & feature alignment
18:15 Maya Chen: product roadmap coming up: new autoscaler improvements (Q2), better KV cache eviction heuristics, and more quantized model variants. Also an observability dashboard change to break down token costs per route.
18:33 Priya Nair: the dashboard change will be really helpful for product owners.
18:38 Liam Patel: also we're adding a canary rollout for model updates so you can keep older variants until quality is validated.

20:00 Security/compliance notes
20:05 Sofia Martinez: security question — we're under a SOC 2 audit next month. Can you confirm data retention and KMS integration?
20:15 Maya Chen: yes, Redwood supports customer KMS with envelope encryption and you can set retention policies; we'll share SOC 2 report and architecture docs.
20:28 Ethan Cole: also need SSO/SAML integration details for RBAC.
20:35 Janelle Ortiz: I'll send the SSO integration guide and the customer-managed SAML metadata.

22:10 Proposal: Dedicated pool test
22:15 Maya Chen: given the incidents and peak needs, we suggest a 2-week dedicated pilot for your nightly reindex and peak chat flows. This would let you measure p95 improvements and cost per token under dedicated pricing.
22:40 Sofia Martinez: what's the expected delta in unit cost?
22:45 Maya Chen: depends on utilization; if you achieve steady throughput during the index window, effective cost per embedding could drop 20-40% due to better packing and reserved capacity. We'll model it in the sizing doc.
22:58 Ethan Cole: what's the onboarding time for Dedicated on a VPC?
23:05 Maya Chen: typically 3-5 business days for initial setup once contracts are signed and peering is scheduled.

25:00 Technical follow-ups
25:05 Liam Patel: action items — we'll run the KV cache benchmark with your sample dataset and share results; we'll also test quantized embedder on your eval set.
25:20 Priya Nair: great — for the benchmark we can provide a smaller subset of the index (10k items) and the traffic replay.
25:30 Ethan Cole: I'll dump the traffic replay and SSO logs to the secure bucket and share the link.

27:00 Open Q&A
27:05 Sofia Martinez: on contracts, if we commit to a 6-month Dedicated contract and we need to scale up, how does billing work?
27:18 Maya Chen: you can add burst credits or increase capacity; contract amendments prorate the change. We'll include options in the proposal.
27:30 Priya Nair: any concerns about vendor lock-in?
27:35 Maya Chen: we support model version pinning and exportable logs/artifacts; we also provide standardized APIs so you can move between hosted and dedicated with minimal code changes.

31:00 Recap & next steps
31:05 Maya Chen: recap — Redwood to send Dedicated pilot proposal and updated pricing, SE to run KV cache and quantized embedder benchmarks, Aperture to share traffic replay and grant access to the sample dataset, CSM to provide SOC 2 and SSO docs.
31:30 Sofia Martinez: that sounds right. Please include a clear estimate for expected p95 improvements and cost delta in the deck.
31:45 Janelle Ortiz: will do — I'll attach the incident tickets and the QBR deck after the call.

34:00 Closing
34:05 Maya Chen: thanks everyone; we'll follow up with the proposal by Friday.
34:12 Ethan Cole: thanks, talk soon.
34:15 Priya Nair: thanks all.

Artifacts shared post-call:
- QBR deck (link): https://redwood.app/qbr/aperture-2026-03

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-heard terms: "KV cache" sometimes transcribed as "KV cash", "quantized" as "quantize". Speaker labels are mostly accurate, with a couple of short cross-talks.

End of transcript.
